content.text: I couldn't read any file contents, so this diagnosis is inferred from the symptom and the file layout. I haven't confirmed it against the code.

candidates.explanation: Most likely cause. The guard decides who gets 403 on admin-only endpoints. Only the seeded first account passes, so the check probably ties access to something specific to that user instead of the role. Examples are comparing the user's id or the first role id, or comparing the wrong values, such as the user id against RoleEnum.admin (1), or a type mismatch between a numeric role id and a string. The check should compare request.user.role.id, as a string, against the roles required by @Roles.

The JWT payload is turned into request.user here. If it drops or mis-maps the role, for example by using the user id as the role or not carrying role.id through, the guard sees the wrong role for every user except the first.
The @Roles(...) decorator or the guard setup on the controller may be wrong. If the roles metadata is wrong or the guards are applied in the wrong order, admin-only routes would reject valid admins.

fix.description: Make canActivate read the required roles from the @Roles metadata. Compare them to the authenticated user's role id, with both sides cast to the same type: `return roles.map(String).includes(String(request.user?.role?.id));`. Remove any check on the user id or a hardcoded id. Also confirm that JwtStrategy.validate returns a user object that includes `role`.
